Thanks again for the call today — great overview of Finex's streaming summarization flow. Recap and a few follow-ups (so we're aligned before Rafael does a sizing pass):

Summary of what you shared:

- Average response size: ~120 tokens (range 60-300 depending on call length).
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end generation <= 200 ms for the streaming use case (front-end shows progressive updates).
- Concurrency target: steady state ~20 concurrent users generating at once; expected peak concurrency up to ~80 (30 min daily spikes).
- Steady QPS: ~10 requests/sec; peak QPS: bursts up to ~40 req/sec for ~20-30 minutes.
- Streaming: chunked streaming is used; clients will accept partial token flushes at ~64-token chunks.

Open questions for sizing (please confirm):
1) Is 120 tokens the average for the final response, or the average tokens produced per streaming session (i.e., sum of chunks)?
2) Can you share a small sample of request/response sizes and the timestamped QPS profile (CSV works).
3) Any hard P50/P90/P95 latency targets from the UI side besides the p95 <= 200 ms?

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Thanks Alex — got the CSV, useful sample. I ran a quick back-of-envelope sizing and included assumptions below. Attaching a short PDF with the math (redwood_throughput_estimate.pdf).

Assumptions from dataset + call:
- Average tokens per final response: 120 tokens (confirmed).
- Steady QPS: 10 req/s; peak QPS: 40 req/s (30-min daily spikes).
- Concurrency: steady 20 concurrent sessions, peak 80 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming chunk size: 64 tokens (client shows partial updates).

Sizing calculations (high level):
- Steady-state tokens/sec = 10 req/s * 120 tokens = 1,200 tokens/sec.
- Peak tokens/sec = 40 req/s * 120 tokens = 4,800 tokens/sec.
- With streaming/chunking, server will produce tokens in bursts; effective simultaneous token emission during a peak could be higher depending on chunk alignment — plan for a 1.5x buffer -> ~7,200 tokens/sec as safety upper bound.

Preliminary infra guidance (options):
1) Dedicated (predictable p95): 1-2 H100-class GPUs for pilot with model 13B quantized; for 70B consider 2x H100 with model sharding. H100 tends to give better single-request latency for large models, but 13B quantized on A100 (80GB) is very cost effective and simpler for steady throughput.
2) Hosted multi-instance: autoscale target pools with warm KV cache + prefix caching to keep p95 under 200ms during bursts; suggest aggressive pre-warming during expected spike windows.

Redwood runtime recommendations to meet p95 <= 200ms:
- Use continuous batching but cap batch window to <10ms for streaming endpoints to avoid batching-induced tail latency.
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated assistant prompts to cut repeated compute.
- Flush partial tokens to client as soon as chunk reaches ~32-64 tokens to satisfy progressive UI updates.

Questions that will materially change sizing:
- Model choice (13B quantized vs 70B) — 70B increases tokens/sec cost and memory footprint considerably.
- Exact percentiles on token generation time per token (if you have microsecond-level traces).

Next steps:
- I'll refine numbers and provide a short config + cost delta matrix after a brief run against the CSV (will do a sample inference run and report GPU tokens/sec curves).
- Proposal: 30-min sizing review Wed 31 Mar 09:00 PT — can you confirm?

Attachment: redwood_throughput_estimate.pdf (3 pages) — includes calculations above and a recommended starting configuration.
